title: docs: Zod 4.6 announcement post
body:
The 4.6 announcement post, following the 4.5 skeleton: at-a-glance links, a section per feature, a `Bug fixes` section of ⚠️ entries, then the commit roll-up (50 commits).

`z.properties()` moves here from the 4.5 post. It shipped in 4.5 as an array of checks, which could assert but never narrow; #6536 made it a schema with a `.properties()` method on `z.instanceof()`. The version a reader goes looking for is the 4.6 one, so the highlight belongs here. The #5912 line stays in the 4.5 commit list — that commit did ship in 4.5.

Every before/after line is checked against the published `zod@4.5.4` and a `main` checkout: the `.options` ordering on a numeric enum, the emoji and `fromJSONSchema` cases, the locale swapped between parse and read, and the spread arity change behind the `z.properties()` callout.

The two perf sections carry prose numbers rather than charts. The machine has been above load 15 for the whole session, which is well over the threshold `AGENTS.md` sets for a publishable figure — the charts want a quiet box and can land separately.

The banner moves to 4.6, as it did for 4.5 in #6481. Merge this immediately before cutting the release, not before.

#6547 has landed as 62e6624b, so the `.validate()` section stays and the roll-up is 51 commits.

The roll-up is current as of 62e6624b and wants one more regenerate immediately before merge, since anything landing between now and the release changes both the list and the count.

The new harness does not reproduce this bound for compiled schemas: on two idle-runner runs its compiled valid-input table reported `1.1x–1.9x` and `1.2x–2.2x`, both with a `1.6x` median, while only the plain table stayed near parity. Please distinguish plain from compiled valid-input behavior instead of saying the failure path is the only divergence.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Valid-input performance differs after compilation

## Affected sites
- packages/docs/content/blog/zod-4-6.mdx:94 — combines the plain and compiled cases into one `0.9x–1.3x` claim
- packages/bench/validate-vs-safeparse.ts:228-255 — reports separate plain and compiled valid-input ranges

## Required outcome
- Make the guidance match reproducible benchmark output and state plain and compiled valid-input behavior separately.

## Suggested approach
- Keep the near-parity guidance for plain schemas, and note that compiled `.validate()` can also be materially faster on accepted input.
````

+author: Colin McDonnell

+import { Accordion, Accordions } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/accordion';
+import { Tabs, Tab } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';
+
+Zod 4.6 is now available.
+
+```sh
+npm install zod@latest
+```
+
+At a glance:
+
+- [`z.instanceof().properties()`](#zproperties) — validates properties of an instance
+- [`.validate()`](#validate) — checks input validity without building a result (up to 35x faster than `.safeParse().success` on a compiled schema)
+- [`fromJSONSchema()`](#fromjsonschema) — enforces six validation keywords it used to ignore
+
+## `z.properties()`
+
+A new API for validating specific properties of an object. Unlike `z.object()` it validates *in-place*, so it plays nice with class instances. ([#6536](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6536))
+
+```ts
+const responseLike = z.properties({ status: z.number().min(200).max(299) });
+
+responseLike.parse(new Response("ok", { status: 200 }));  // ✅ a real Response
+responseLike.parse({ status: 204 });                      // ✅ a plain object
+```
+
+A corresponding `.properties()` method has been added to `ZodInstanceof`.

- Keep the 4.5 and 4.6 announcements accurate about which release introduced each API and optimization.

A method call like `Player.safeParse(data)` never reads the exports object, and the ESM build is unchanged. + +## Memory retention in recursive schemas + +A recursive schema held the input and output of its last parse until the next parse replaced it, so one long-lived schema pinned every object it had touched. Zod 4.4 released that input and Zod 4.5 did not, which surfaced as an out-of-memory failure on a repository-wide lint run. ([#6572](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6572)) + +```ts +const Category = z.object({ + name: z.string(), + get children() { + return z.array(Category); + }, +}); +``` + +## Bug fixes + +### ⚠️ Error maps run on the first read of `error` + +Because `safeParse()` now builds its error lazily, error maps — global, locale, and per-schema `error` — run when `result.error` is first read, not at parse time. ([#6519](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6519)) + +```ts +const result = schema.safeParse(12); +z.config(z.locales.fr()); +result.error.issues[0].message; // French in 4.6, English in 4.5 +``` + +An error map with a side effect never runs if nothing reads the error. ([#6532](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6532)) + +```ts +z.emoji().parse("😀"); // ✅ +z.emoji().parse("1️⃣"); // ✅ the keycap is the anchor +z.emoji().parse("123"); // ❌ was accepted in 4.5 +``` + +Flags, subdivision flags, skin-tone-modified emoji, and ZWJ sequences are unchanged. The parser already ignored those keys, but `.options` was read straight off the enum object, so a three-member enum listed six values and three of them failed to parse. ([#6542](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6542)) + +```ts +enum Country { UK, Germany, France } + +z.enum(Country).options; // 4.5: ["UK", "Germany", "France", 0, 1, 2] — 4.6: [0, 1, 2] +``` + +### ⚠️ base64 patterns + +The runtime patterns for `z.base64()` and `z.base64url()` are the character sets, with length and padding enforced in code, so a multi-megabyte string can no longer overflow the regex stack through a composed schema. The JSON Schema output still emits the exact block forms, so `z.toJSONSchema()` is unchanged. ([#6534](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6534), [#6527](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6527)) + +Composing `z.base64()` into a template literal now checks the alphabet but not the length, which is how `z.creditCard()` already behaves there. ([#6573](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6573)) + +The pattern is visible in three other places. `z.regexes.email` has no capture groups now, and neither of the two it used to expose held a usable value.
